prompt:
A desktop landing page for the website "I fucking hate snaps.", rendered edge to edge at 1536x1024 landscape with crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it.

The site collects real, anonymous complaints about Ubuntu snaps. This is the front door: it shows no quotes, only the way in. Very sparse and calm: lots of empty warm off-white space, very few elements, one thing to do.

Visual law: clean flat vector illustration with crisp edges, like a well-made web illustration. No grain, no halftone, no risograph texture, no paper texture, no gloss, no gradients, no shadows beyond a flat hole shape, no 3D. No radiating rays or burst lines. No navigation bar, no coffee or donation link. Content in reading order: the headline "I fucking hate snaps." in heavy black type; three black oval holes in a row; the line "Whack a snap." in black; a small underlined link "Report your own".

What leads: the whack-a-mole game. From the middle hole stands tall a chunky paper-origami bird made of three or four big flat triangles in a dull grey-green with a small black triangular beak, an obvious parody that is clearly not any real logo: rounder proportions, a proud face: chest puffed out, beak raised, eyes contentedly closed and a self-satisfied grin. The only red on the page is a tiny accent on the link underline.
